scenes.heading: Understanding Cerebral Palsy
scenes.body: A short guide for parents and families.

scenes.heading: What is cerebral palsy?
scenes.body: Cerebral palsy, or CP, is a group of conditions that affect how a child moves, balances and holds their body.

scenes.heading: It begins in the developing brain
scenes.body: CP happens when the part of the brain that guides movement is injured or develops differently, before, during or soon after birth.

scenes.heading: Every child is different
scenes.body: CP looks different in each child. Some need a little support, others need more.
bullets: Some children walk on their own
Some use a walker or a wheelchair

scenes.heading: Signs to look out for
scenes.body: Talk to a doctor if your baby:
bullets: Feels very stiff or very floppy
Is late to hold their head up, roll or sit
Mostly uses one side of the body

scenes.heading: Trust what you notice
scenes.body: You know your child best. If something worries you, ask a doctor. The earlier, the better.

scenes.heading: Early support helps
scenes.body: Therapy that starts early helps children build strength, movement and everyday skills.

scenes.heading: Tools that open doors
scenes.body: Walkers, wheelchairs and braces help children move, explore and join in.

scenes.heading: Many ways to communicate
scenes.body: Some children talk with words. Others use gestures, pictures or a tablet. Every voice matters.

scenes.heading: Learning, playing, belonging
scenes.body: Children with CP go to school, make friends and love to play. Inclusion helps every child grow.

scenes.heading: You are not alone
scenes.body: Doctors, therapists, teachers and other families can walk this journey with you.
bullets: Ask about early support near you

scenes.heading: Every child can shine
scenes.body: With love, support and opportunity, children with cerebral palsy can thrive. For awareness, not medical advice.
